sampling_model.design: Superpopulation observational sampling with no parametric model for the categorical distribution, propensities, or outcome regressions.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment \(A\) with identification by consistency and conditional exchangeability given \(X\).
sampling_model.overlap: Fixed \(\epsilon\le P(A=1\mid X=k)\le1-\epsilon\) on every positive-mass category.
sampling_model.outcome: Real outcomes with \(|\mu_{ak}|\le M\) and explicitly imposed unstandardized conditional fourth central moments at most \(M^4\); this implies conditional variances at most \(M^2\) but imposes no standardized-kurtosis or positive-variance condition.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The cross-fitted saturated-cell propensities and outcome regressions are explicit and have weighted squared-error order \(d_n/n\) on the balanced local class. The global pilot-selected light factorial statistic is explicit only through the banked compatibility handle; the proposed heavy robust score remains to be defined.
sampling_model.computation: Categorical and treatment coordinates are exact and real outcomes have dyadic enclosures. Coefficient and falling-factorial recurrences admit outward interval evaluation, but certified monotone bisection is not currently available because the stipulated symmetric half-log score is nonmonotone and can have zero derivative; a retained monotone bracket or a corrected score is required.
sampling_model.randomness: All probabilities and expectations are under the observed iid sample law \(Q_P^{(n)}=P_O^{\otimes n}\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2 on pages 8--10 lower-bounds worst-case mean squared error for the one-arm functional \(\psi_1\) by the order of \(n^{-1}+d^2/[n^2\log^2 n]\) under fixed overlap; Appendix C.5 sets the control-arm regression to zero in the hard family.
The paper constructs heavy-light best-polynomial factorial-moment estimators attaining minimax mean squared error for additive discrete-distribution functionals.

Sections 4.1--4.2 provide scalar bounded-influence score inequalities, but they do not prove a tail theorem for this pilot-selected marked-factorial statistic; moreover, the symmetric half-log transform stipulated in the current directive is not globally monotone and therefore needs an additional retained-range or score replacement before root inversion is valid.
Theorem 1 lower-bounds expected confidence length in Gaussian nonparametric experiments by a between-class modulus and the paper constructs constant-factor adaptive intervals.
Theorem 5.1 gives uniformly valid asymptotically efficient Gaussian ATE intervals from cross-fitted orthogonal scores under nuisance-rate conditions.

The Abstract and Sections 2--4 derive finite-sample optimal bias-aware ATE estimators and confidence intervals under smoothness or shape restrictions when regression errors are normal with known variance, with feasible asymptotic extensions for unknown errors.

Theorem 3.1 gives a self-normalized moderate-deviation expansion for fixed-order nondegenerate Studentized U-statistics under moment conditions; its degree-one consequence is used only for the oracle-score central limit step.
The paper gives nearly tight dimension-free confidence intervals for probabilities of individually unobserved multinomial events.

body.tldr: The identified ATE and the banked four-coordinate light-cell approximation are valid, and this round proves the regular balanced-submodel expansion, variance consistency, and Gaussian limit for the explicit cross-fitted saturated one-step estimator. The proposed globally honest heavy-light interval is not yet a theorem: its rare-cell score uses a symmetric half-log transform that is not globally monotone, while its heavy branch and Gaussian/fallback hybrid are not explicit sample maps. Therefore the uniform upper frontier, certified numerical interval, and heavy-light endpoint equivalence remain open rather than being inferred from the banked mean-squared-error calculation.

project_justification.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024 supplies the large-alphabet point-risk obstruction and documents uncertain Gaussian/bootstrap coverage in the \(n=9915,d=8196\) 401(k) application, but not an honest expected-length theorem. The accepted heterogeneity run supplies the one-mark factorial approximation and bias architecture, not a direct confidence-tail calibration. Catoni2012 supplies scalar score inequalities; it does not validate the nonmonotone symmetric half-log root prescribed here or control the common-pilot fluctuation of a selected factorial statistic.
project_justification.niche: The unresolved contribution is an explicit globally honest interval for arbitrary categorical cell masses under fixed overlap and an absolute conditional fourth-moment envelope, together with a same-class confidence-length converse and a certified implementation. Any valid construction must calibrate the selected light statistic and the heavy branch directly, while switching to the efficient Gaussian radius on the balanced local regime.
project_justification.fill: The present core proves the imported light approximation bias and now proves the saturated one-step Gaussian benchmark under \(d_n=o(\sqrt n)\). It also isolates a concrete obstruction to the proposed calibration: the stipulated half-log score is redescending, can have several roots, and has no uniform slope for bisection. Completing the project requires replacing that score or proving a retained-range theorem, controlling pilot-dependent centering, and defining the heavy winsorized self-normalized Gaussian/fallback branch before the global, numerical, and endpoint claims can be restored.

body.related_work: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024 remains the application and point-risk anchor: it treats arbitrary categorical masses, gives the one-arm large-alphabet lower rate, and reports the \(n=9915,d=8196\) 401(k) saturated analysis, but does not prove the present honest-length frontier. CausalSmithHeterogeneityFrontier2026 supplies the clipped real-mark Chebyshev factorial estimator and its bias/second-moment architecture; no tail theorem is imported from it. Catoni2012 provides scalar bounded-influence score inequalities, but the symmetric half-log formula stipulated in this run is redescending rather than globally monotone, so the source does not justify unique-root inversion here. ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML and Hahn1998 supply the regular efficient ATE benchmark; the narrowed local theorem verifies the required saturated-cell nuisance rates directly on the project-imposed balanced class. ShaoZhou2016 is used only for the degree-one oracle-score normal limit and does not cover the growing-degree selected factorial statistic. ArmstrongKolesar2021, CaiLow2004, and Painsky2022 remain adjacent comparators rather than sources of the missing global construction.
body.technical_internal_limitation: For the stipulated symmetric score, direct differentiation gives \(\psi'(x)=2(2-x^2)/(x^4+4)\). It is increasing only for \(|x|<\sqrt2\), decreases outside that range, tends back to zero in both tails, and can produce at least three roots for an odd collection of block values. Consequently uniqueness, monotone bisection, and a uniform score-to-root error modulus are false without an additional retained-range theorem. The common pilot creates a second issue: conditional block calibration is centered at a pilot-dependent mean, whereas the open target is centered at the unconditional expectation.
body.honest_scope: The global model continues to allow arbitrary and zero cell masses, fixed overlap, bounded cell means, and only an absolute conditional fourth-central-moment envelope; no standardized-kurtosis or positive cell-variance condition is added. Under those same assumptions, only the light approximation bias and the balanced-submodel saturated one-step limit are currently established. No finite-sample heavy-light coverage, sharp expected length, certified endpoint computation, or heavy-light Gaussian endpoint equivalence is claimed until the rare and heavy score constructions are made explicit and proved. The balanced mass and nondegenerate efficient-variance conditions remain local restrictions only.
body.interpretation: On a balanced table with \(d_n=o(\sqrt n)\), the ordinary cross-fitted saturated one-step estimator has the familiar efficient Gaussian limit and a ratio-consistent score variance. This does not yet license reporting the proposed heavy-light interval: global honesty at the rare-cell transition still depends on a valid directly calibrated score and an explicit heavy branch.
